output.summary: KEP-2436 proposes a migration mechanism for HA clusters moving cloud-specific controllers from kube-controller-manager to cloud-controller-manager, using secondary leader-election locks shared between the two components. Status is implemented, stage stable.
output.rationale: SIG Cloud Provider is extracting in-tree cloud code and removing it from kube-controller-manager, so existing HA clusters need a low-risk way to switch. The KEP adds a primary lock plus configurable secondary migration locks so only one component runs a given cloud controller at a time, including across version skew. The source says this path is for clusters with very strict availability requirements, and that clusters that can tolerate downtime should disable in-tree providers and deploy the CCM instead.

alternatives.option: Take the control plane down, reconfigure components to use the CCM, then bring it back up
alternatives.why_not: The KEP says this is suitable only where downtime is tolerable; it is not acceptable for environments with strict uptime requirements, which is the case this KEP targets.

alternatives.option: Change every controller so two instances of the same controller can run in KCM and CCM at once
alternatives.why_not: The KEP calls this a massive change to all controllers that may need other synchronization, and says the controller manager should provide the migration mechanism instead of each controller.

The KEP's drawbacks note that if downtime is allowed, KCM and CCM need no migration mechanism; for strict-uptime clusters, without coordination, the same controller could run in both places during upgrade.

evidence.quote: This KEP proposes a mechanism in which HA clusters can safely migrate “cloud specific” controllers between the kube-controller-manager and the cloud-controller-manager via a shared resource lock between the two components.

If a cluster can tolerate short intervals of downtime, it is recommended to update your cluster with in-tree cloud providers disabled, and then deploy the respective out-of-tree cloud-controller-manager.
this KEP proposes a _primary_ and N configurable _secondary_ (a.k.a migration) leader election locks in the KCM and the CCM.
Change all controllers so that they can handle a situation where two instances of the same controller are running in both KCM and CCM.
